articles.title: Ed Barnard: The Warwickshire captain who 'commands respect'
articles.summary: How Shropshire lad Ed Barnard skippered Warwickshire to a title triumph in his first season as a county captain.
articles.body:
Behind every great team there is generally a great leader and Warwickshire's County Championship winning captain Ed Barnard is the latest to fit that particular bill.

To take over as skipper just a fortnight before the start of a new season , then lead your team to the Championship is the stuff of dreams.

For Barney's Bears to do it in the manner they did, winning their final four games, three of them by an innings, makes the 2026 title race take on even more legendary status.

From the moment red-ball cricket returned in August, Warwickshire won five matches and drew the other.

The first of those victories, a desperately tense one-wicket win over Sussex marshalled by last pair Chris Woakes and Olly Hannon-Dalby, was probably the one inspirational trigger point of the Bears' charge to the title.

But the coolest man on and off the field as the drama hotted up was 30-year-old Barnard, the Shropshire-born former Worcestershire all-rounder, who swapped the Pears for the Bears at the end of the 2022 season.

"He's just so consistent both as a player and a person," Warwickshire first-team coach Ian Westwood told BBC Radio WM.

"He's made my job so simple this year, with the high standards he sets and the way he leads from the front with bat and ball. He commands the respect of everyone in he changing room because of who he is."

Bears beat Leicestershire to secure ninth title

The Bears' necessity: Just how good is top wicket-taker Bamber?

There was also a lovely irony that, having won his only previous trophy as a Worcestershire player in 2018 - the T20 Blast - in beating Leicestershire last weekend, also at Edgbaston, Barnard was again in the company of the Pears' dual matchwinner that day, Ben Cox, now the Foxes wicketkeeper. A pair of once young tyros now all grown up!

The crucial run of four straight wins in September, also at Southampton, Cardiff and Chelmsford, was what catapulted Warwickshire from outsiders to a ninth title.

"Over the last month we've been exceptional," added Westwood.

"It seemed a long time to wait from winning at Chelmsford to getting the last game started and, when it became ours to lose, it added to the pressure. But Ed and the lads dealt with it all superbly."

Westwood - a Warwickshire title winner himself in 2012 - also acknowledges the part played by returning bowling coach Graeme 'Pop' Welch and Sussex-bound batting coach Matthew Walker .

"The bowling has got lots of plaudits and rightly so. Ethan Bamber, Woakesey [Chris Woakes] and Olly [Hannon-Dalby] have been brilliant and Manny Suthar has come in and given us just what we need," Westwood said.

"But we've done really well with the bat. We've played on a lot of bowler-friendly pitches and still scored the runs we needed."

All spearheaded by 1,048 runs from Sam Hain, at a stunning average of almost 75, a genuine beacon of consistency as he passed 50 in 10 of his 13 matches (two tons and eight half-centuries).

"Sam Hain has been like a man possessed," said Westwood. "He's the leader of that batting group. We couldn't have done it without him."

Barnard managed one unprecedented achievement when he lifted the trophy on Saturday afternoon - he became the first cricketer from Shropshire to do it.

Plenty of Shropshire-born players have gone on to enjoy good first-class careers.

One of them, Oswestry's Andy Lloyd, even opened the batting for England. Both Barnard and Joe Clarke played for England at Under-19 and Lions level before becoming sidelined, for differing reasons.

But then Barnard is from particularly strong Minor Counties-bred stock.

Not only was he born in a Minor County, in the county town Shrewsbury, his elder brother Mike also played for Shropshire and they were the sons of a Minor Counties player.

Their father, Andy, held a coaching role both at Shrewsbury Cricket Club and in the cricket academy at Shrewsbury School under former Worcestershire paceman Paul Pridgeon - the latter a production line that has also churned out the likes of James Taylor, Joe Leach, Issy Wong and Dillon Pennington.

Barnard Snr was also part of the most famous day in the county's cricketing history back in 1984, when he took the last three wickets as Shropshire famously turned over mighty Yorkshire, starring Geoffrey Boycott (c & b Brian Perry 27, for the record), in the first round of the NatWest Trophy.

Now Barnard Jr's efforts this summer have helped put Proud Salopia right back on the cricket map.

articles.title: ‘If he thinks about 100 centuries’: Ajinkya Rahane reveals if Virat Kohli can reach the milestone
articles.summary: Virat Kohli's latest ODI masterclass has once again brought the possibility of him reaching 100 international centuries into focus, with former India
articles.body: Virat Kohli's latest ODI masterclass has once again brought the possibility of him reaching 100 international centuries into focus, with former India teammate Ajinkya Rahane backing the veteran batter to achieve the landmark if he sets his mind to it.Kohli produced a spectacular unbeaten 139 off 88 balls in the first ODI against West Indies, powering India to an eight-wicket victory while chasing 296 with 50 balls to spare. The 37-year-old struck nine sixes, the most he has hit in a single innings in his career, on his way to his 55th ODI century and 86th international hundred.While Kohli has made it clear that personal milestones are not what drive him, Rahane believes the former India captain's ability to put pressure on himself could help him chase down the elusive three-figure mark.“I think when Virat Kohli puts pressure on himself, that is when he is at his best. In every innings, he has done that. He has those expectations of himself. That is why he has been able to do it consistently for so many years," Rahane said on Cricbuzz.Kohli's attacking approach has also become increasingly evident since his retirement from Test cricket. The batter has shown a greater willingness to take risks early in his innings, rather than spending a longer period settling in.Before 2025, Kohli's strike rate during the first 10 balls of his innings was a little above 72. That figure has now climbed beyond 100. The first signs of the change were visible during the series against South Africa, and he has continued with the more aggressive approach since then.With Kohli now playing only ODI cricket for India, he has roughly 30 matches remaining to score another 14 centuries and reach 100 international hundreds. Only Sachin Tendulkar has previously achieved the landmark.Rahane feels there is no reason for Kohli to shy away from thinking about the target, particularly given Tendulkar's influence on his career."Knowing Virat, if he thinks about 100 centuries, there is nothing wrong with it, because his role model has been Sachin Tendulkar. So, I am sure he must be thinking about it. If he thinks about it, only Virat Kohli can achieve that,” he added.Rahane also rejected the idea that a batter thinking about a statistical milestone necessarily means he is putting individual achievement ahead of the team.“Many times, we think that if a player is thinking about milestones, that means he is selfish. But when Virat Kohli puts pressure on himself, that is when he does well. So, I am sure he will have a number on his mind, but at the same time, he will also have the thought that he has to enjoy the game as long as he is playing,” said Rahane.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mohit Sharma set to join CSK as bowling coach
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former India bowler Mohit Sharma is set to join the Zaheer Khan-led Chennai Super Kings (CSK) support staff as the bowling coach starting next
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India bowler Mohit Sharma is set to join the Zaheer Khan-led Chennai Super Kings (CSK) support staff as the bowling coach starting next season.The development was confirmed by CSK CEO Kasi Viswanathan. "Mohit will join CSK as our new bowling coach. His name was recommended by our head coach Zaheer Khan. Mohit was tremendous with us as a player as well and we hope he will do a great job as bowling coach," Viswanathan told TimesofIndia.com."The next set of coaching staffs will also be recruited on Zaheer's recommendation in the coming weeks," he added.Mohit last played in the Indian Premier League (IPL) for the Delhi Capitals but has had two stints with CSK previously, spanning four seasons. He replaces Eric Simmons as the bowling coach.The 38-year-old Mohit has played 120 fixtures in the IPL and has 134 wickets to his name. He had a second wind of sorts during his time at Gujarat Titans, where he emerged as the side's consistent wicket-taker due to his variety and accuracy. Sharma picked up 41 wickets in the two seasons he spent at GT. He also represented Punjab Kings from 2016 to 2018.The Haryana bowler announced his retirement from professional cricket in December last year."Today, with a full heart, I announce my retirement from all formats of cricket. From representing Haryana to wearing the India jersey and playing in the IPL, this journey has been nothing short of a blessing.""A very special thank you to the Haryana Cricket Association for being the backbone of my career. And my deepest gratitude to Anirudh Sir, whose constant guidance and belief in me shaped my path in ways words cannot express. Thank you to the BCCI, my coaches, my teammates, IPL franchises, support staff and all my friends for their love and support," Mohit wrote in an emotional retirement post.His journey with the Indian team will be remembered for the 2015 World Cup under MS Dhoni, where he was the joint third-highest wicket-taker. As far as the IPL is concerned, 2014 was his best outing — he won the Purple Cap after taking 23 wickets — and it came in CSK's colours.Mohit has played 26 ODIs and eight T20Is for India and picked up 31 and six wickets, respectively.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ILT20 Auction: Babar Azam, Phil Salt, Wanindu Hasaranga among T20 stars set for Season 5 auction
articles.summary: Babar Azam, Phil Salt, Wanindu Hasaranga, Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Liam Livingstone, Faf du Plessis and Alzarri Joseph are among the leading names in the
articles.body: Babar Azam, Phil Salt, Wanindu Hasaranga, Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Liam Livingstone, Faf du Plessis and Alzarri Joseph are among the leading names in the player pool for the DP World ILT20 Season 5 auction, which will be held in Dubai on October 1.More than 200 players from 23 countries have been shortlisted for the auction, which will take place at the ICC Academy Indoors from 1pm GST (2:30pm IST). The six franchises will use the auction to complete their squads ahead of the 34-match season, which runs from November 21 to December 20.The player pool includes representatives from 11 ICC Full Member nations, along with cricketers from ILT20 partners Kuwait and Saudi Arabia and 10 other Associate Member nations.Players have been divided into three base-price categories of $80,000, $40,000 and $10,000.The highest bracket features several established T20 names, including Babar, Salt, Banton, Gurbaz, Hasaranga, Livingstone, du Plessis, Joseph, Jonny Bairstow, Moeen Ali, Alex Hales, Naseem Shah, Fazalhaq Farooqi and Chris Woakes.Several players in the top bracket featured in Season 4, with Salt having represented Abu Dhabi Knight Riders, Banton turning out for MI Emirates and Gurbaz playing for Gulf Giants. Bairstow, Moeen and Hales were also part of the previous season.The $40,000 bracket includes Shadab Khan, Ibrahim Zadran, Jayden Seales, Tabraiz Shamsi, Kusal Perera, Gulbadin Naib and Andre Fletcher, while the $10,000 pool features players such as Will Smeed, Reeza Hendricks, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Ish Sodhi, George Munsey and Matt Potts.UAE players could attract strong interestThe auction will also be significant for UAE cricket, with all UAE, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia players entering at a base price of $10,000.Under the Season 5 recruitment rules, none of the players from those three countries could be retained by their previous franchises. That leaves several established UAE internationals, including Muhammad Waseem, Junaid Siddique, Haider Ali, Ayan Afzal Khan, Alishan Sharafu and Khuzaima Tanveer, available for selection.Each franchise will also have one Right to Match option, which can be used on a UAE player who represented the team in Season 4 or featured for the franchise in the recently concluded ILT20 Development Tournament.The playing XI regulations will further increase the importance of the local player pool. Every team must field at least two UAE players, two Afghanistan players and one additional Associate Member player in every match.MI Emirates have biggest purseMI Emirates will enter the auction with the biggest purse at $1.39 million, followed by Abu Dhabi Knight Riders with $1.365 million. Desert Vipers and Gulf Giants have $1.305 million each, while Dubai Capitals and Sharjah Warriorz have $1.3 million.Each franchise is required to finish with between 18 and 23 players. Squads must include at least 11 players from ICC Full Member countries, four UAE players, one Kuwait player, one Saudi Arabia player and at least one additional Associate Member player.Teams must spend at least $1.5 million and can spend a maximum of $2 million. They will also be allowed one wildcard signing after the auction for a maximum fee of $250,000.The franchises have already made their pre-auction signings, with Finn Allen, Jason Holder and Sunil Narine among those secured by Abu Dhabi Knight Riders; Marcus Stoinis and Mustafizur Rahman by Dubai Capitals; and David Miller and Heinrich Klaasen by Gulf Giants.Defending champions Desert Vipers have retained Andries Gous and Dan Lawrence while adding Mujeeb-ur-Rahman and Shimron Hetmyer. MI Emirates have kept Nicholas Pooran, Rashid Khan and Romario Shepherd and added Sherfane Rutherford.Sharjah Warriorz have signed Adam Milne, James Vince and Waqar Salamkheil, while retaining Sikandar Raza.The Season 5 auction will be streamed on the ILT20 YouTube channel, with viewers in India able to watch it on Zee5. articles.title: Test cricket's biggest scandals: Rank BBC Sport's top 10
articles.summary: As memories of sandpapergate are rekindled by Australia's upcoming tour of South Africa, rank the biggest scandals in Test cricket's history.
articles.body:
Australia are due to play their first Test in South Africa since the sandpapergate scandal rocked the cricketing world eight years ago.

To mark one of the biggest controversies the game has ever seen, Test Match Special is asking which is Test cricket's biggest scandal.

Ten of the most famous scandals in Test cricket have been picked out by a TMS panel and we are asking you to rank them in order of how big they were.

Results of the vote will be revealed on the TMS podcast and you can read more about each scandal below the following vote.

On the 1932-33 tour of Australia, England needed a plan to stop the great Donald Bradman. Douglas Jardine, England's charismatic captain, came up with a tactic that would change the game forever: Bodyline.

Jardine instructed his fast bowlers, Harold Larwood and Bill Voce, to bowl hostile, short-pitched deliveries at the Australians. In an era when batters wore no upper-body protection, England's method was criticised as unsporting and against the spirit of cricket.

The bad blood between the two teams escalated to the administrators of the game in each country and even turned into a diplomatic incident, threatening to strain relationships between governments.

England won the series 4-1, a result almost lost in the infamy of the entire episode.

In 1968, England were due to tour South Africa, a country then operating under a system of racial segregation known as apartheid.

In line for selection was Basil D'Oliveira, a mixed-race all-rounder born in South Africa, who had emigrated to and qualified to play for England.

Despite scoring 158 in the final Test of the summer against Australia, D'Oliveira was initially left out of the England squad, only to then be called in as a replacement for the injured Tom Cartwright. His inclusion was criticised in South Africa and the tour was called off little more than a week later.

South Africa played one more Test series – at home to Australia the following year – then spent two decades out of international cricket. In the intervening time, a number of rebel tours to South Africa took place, with huge consequences for the players involved.

Australia were defending the Ashes in England in 1975. The series was shortened to four Tests because of the inaugural men's World Cup earlier in the summer.

At 1-0 down, England had a huge chance to level the series in the third Test at Headingley. At the close of the fourth day, Australia had reached 220-3 in pursuit of 445. A thrilling finish was in prospect.

Overnight, the pitch was vandalised. Holes were dug and oil was poured on the surface. The damage was caused by supporters of George Davis, who had been jailed for armed robbery the previous year. "George Davis is innocent" was written on the wall around the ground.

The Test was abandoned as a draw, meaning Australia retained the urn and ruining the prospect of a decider at The Oval.

Davis was released in 1976 when his conviction was adjudged to be unsafe, and it was overturned entirely on appeal in 2011.

George Davis appeal win sparks Headingley Ashes memories

In the mid-1970s, Kerry Packer, one of the richest men in Australia, wanted to boost the ratings of his Channel Nine TV network with live sport. He approached the Australian Cricket Board with a lucrative offer, one that was rejected in favour of keeping live cricket on the Australian Broadcasting Corporation.

So, Packer created his own product: World Series Cricket. The plan was simple – Packer recruited the best players in the world to stage his own matches.

Most significant was the signing of England captain Tony Greig, who effectively acted as an agent. Greig was stripped of the captaincy and Australia's 1977 Ashes tour of England was overshadowed by the emergence of Packer's outfit.

World Series Cricket lasted for two seasons – 1977-78 and 1978-79 – comprising one-day matches and 'SuperTests' between teams representing Australia, West Indies and a World XI. Meanwhile, traditional cricket rolled on. In 1978-79, England embarked on Ashes tour they won 5-1, beating an Australia side decimated by Packer defections.

Later in 1979, a truce between Packer and the board was brokered, and Nine earned TV rights to the game in Australia. Many of the innovations of WSC – coloured clothing and day-night cricket among them – shaped the game as we know it today.

Sporting Witness: Kerry Packer's cricket revolution

England had already been frustrated by the decisions of a home umpire in losing the first Test on their tour of Pakistan in late 1987.

Shakoor Rana was appointed to stand in the second Test, much to England's displeasure. Rana had previously clashed with New Zealand skipper Jeremy Coney.

On the second day in Faisalabad, Rana was at square leg when he appeared to halt the game to object to one of England captain Mike Gatting's field placements.

Gatting was furious, confronting the official in footage that has been replayed over and over. The following day, Rana refused to take the field, leaving England waiting in the middle for play that did not get under way.

The match eventually resumed on the fourth day and the cancellation of the tour was narrowly avoided, but mistrust and ill-feeling between England and Pakistan lingered for years later.

In the mid-1990s, ball-tampering was the most emotive topic in Test cricket. In 1992, Pakistan's tour of England was overshadowed by allegations and innuendo. Two years later, the England captain found himself at the centre of a similar row.

In the Lord's Test against South Africa, Michael Atherton was caught by TV cameras rubbing dirt on the ball. Atherton's explanation was that he was trying to maintain the condition of the ball, rather than alter it. Trouble was, he told the match referee he was using the dirt to keep his hands dry.

The story was headline news, topped off by a chaotic news conference when Atherton was, in his own words, "fed to the lions". Atherton considered resigning, but escaped with a fine and remained captain for another four years.

Former South Africa captain Hansie Cronje was one of the most revered figures in his country. He was even close to Nelson Mandela.

Yet he became involved with Indian bookmakers and gradually made suggestions to fix matches, or parts of them. Cronje targeted impressionable team-mates to become part of his scheme.

Cronje's most infamous plot came in a dead-rubber fifth Test against England at Centurion Park in 2000. The match had been badly affected by rain, but Cronje was adamant the teams should do all they could to ensure it did not end in a draw.

He negotiated with England skipper Nasser Hussain for both teams to forfeit an innings, leaving the tourists with a final-day run-chase, which they completed. England were unaware, but Cronje had engineered a result.

Cronje confessed months later and would eventually give public testimony at the King Commission. He was banned from cricket for life and was killed in a plane crash in 2002.

Hansie Cronje, match-fixing and plane crash that left a complex legacy

This scandal had roots in past attitudes towards Pakistan cricket and ball-tampering.

Pakistan had already lost the series in England in 2006, yet were cruising to victory in the final Test at The Oval.

However, Australian umpire Darrel Hair, himself no stranger to controversy, asked for the ball to be changed midway through the afternoon session on the fourth day. Ball-tampering was suggested and Pakistan refused to play after tea.

Confusion reigned. Pakistan captain Inzamam-ul-Haq relented and tried to resume the Test, but by then umpire Hair and partner Billy Doctrove had awarded the match to England.

Years of back-and-forth followed, with the result first changed to a draw, then reverted back to an England win. Inzamam was cleared of ball-tampering, while Hair served a ban from officiating. The match remains the only Test in history to have been forfeited.

No-balls deliberately bowled in the 2010 Lord's Test between England and Pakistan ultimately resulted in three of the tourists' players spending time in jail.

A sting by the News of the World newspaper paid a middleman - cricket agent Mazhar Majeed - for details of three no-balls.

Majeed arranged for Pakistan captain Salman Butt and pace bowlers Mohammad Asif and Mohammad Amir to execute the no-balls, then the News of the World broke the story while the Test was still ongoing.

All three players received bans from the International Cricket Council, then were found guilty of conspiracy to cheat at gambling and conspiracy to accept corrupt payments.

Butt was sentenced to two and a half years in prison, Asif a year and Amir, who was aged only 17 at the time of the no-ball plot, six months.

How Pakistan cricket betting scam unfolded

In the third Test of Australia's bad-tempered tour of South Africa in 2018, TV cameras picked up touring fielder Cameron Bancroft appearing to rub the ball with a small, yellow object.

Bancroft, along with captain Steve Smith, admitted to attempting to alter the condition of the ball. Days later, it was revealed Bancroft was using sandpaper.

The outcry engulfed the Australian team and the entire nation. Prime minister Malcolm Turnbull said he was "bitterly disappointed".

Smith was sacked, along with his vice-captain David Warner, the architect of the plot. All of Smith, Warner and Bancroft served lengthy bans from playing for Australia.

Coach Darren Lehmann was cleared of having knowledge of the ball-tampering, but he too resigned.

articles.title: IND vs WI, live streaming: When and where to watch second ODI as India look to seal series
articles.summary: India’s batting remains its biggest strength, but the pace-bowling combination will be a concern when the hosts look to seal the three-match ODI series
articles.body: India’s batting remains its biggest strength, but the pace-bowling combination will be a concern when the hosts look to seal the three-match ODI series against the West Indies in the second game in Guwahati on Wednesday.Virat Kohli will once again be in the spotlight after he rolled back the years with a record-breaking century in the series opener in Thiruvananthapuram. Captain Shubman Gill also scored a hundred as India chased down 296 in under 42 overs.Kuldeep Yadav was another standout performer, taking 4-40 and making crucial strikes to underline his importance to the attack. However, India’s pace department looked less convincing in the absence of Jasprit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya.Mohammed Siraj was left out of the first ODI as India opened the bowling with all-rounder Nitish Kumar Reddy. The move was part of a dress rehearsal for next year’s ODI World Cup, but the experiment did not go according to plan and raised questions about the decision to leave the more experienced Siraj on the bench.India will return to Guwahati with good memories of the venue. They have won both their ODIs at the Barsapara Cricket Stadium, with Kohli scoring centuries in both matches. Rohit Sharma has also scored a century and a half-century at the venue.Batting-friendly conditions could again put the bowlers under pressure. All four innings in the two ODIs played at the venue have produced scores of more than 300, while the bowlers from both teams were put under pressure in the series opener at the Greenfield International Stadium.It remains to be seen whether the Indian management changes the bowling attack for the second ODI. articles.title: Joss Buttler says Brendon McCullum's removal as England Test coach may have boosted Cricket World Cup chances
articles.summary: Brendon McCullum left his role as England Test coach in July; Jos Buttler believes the move has allowed the New Zealander to focus solely on helping England win the Cricket World Cup; Buttler has been ruled out of the upcoming Pakistan white-ball tour due to injury
articles.body:
McCullum was relieved of his red-ball duties in July , with Stephen Fleming eventually named as his successor , but remained in charge of a limited-overs set-up that ended the summer with a record of 11 wins and two defeats.

That included ODI series wins over India and Sri Lanka , raising England's stock in a format that has seen them decline since they became world champions in 2019.

Buttler, who captained the team in their ill-fated 2023 title defence, thinks the split coaching model has allowed McCullum to throw all his energy towards next year's tournament in southern Africa.

"He's only got one focus now and that is the white ball," Buttler said on his For the Love of Cricket podcast.

"It's not that he couldn't do everything, because he could, but your time is more spread and you've got more to think about with the Test team as well.

"Now he can focus solely on white-ball cricket - T20, yes, but mainly ODI cricket with that World Cup on the horizon. It seems like Baz is naturally all in on, 'how do I win this World Cup with this team?'

"I think he can sort of see that World Cup is not that far away. It's a real target, now his remit has changed from four months ago being in charge of everything to, 'right, I can really nail down on this'. He's just got more time and more focus on that.

"ODI cricket for England has not been consistently great for a couple of years, so there's some nice growth to go on that and this summer's been a really good start."

Buttler delivers update on hamstring injury

Buttler is currently sidelined with a hamstring injury and has already been ruled out for the forthcoming tri-series tour of Pakistan.

He is also a doubt for the November trip to Australia, meaning the team's most experienced one-day player could miss as many as eight ODIs and a significant chunk of the pre-World Cup preparations.

"I've had a scan and I'm waiting to see the specialist. Then we'll know what the next steps are," he said.

"The unknown is often the tough part. Any cricketer just wants a physio or a doctor to tell you, 'on this date you'll be back playing cricket'. Unfortunately, they can't do that just yet."

articles.title: Jos Buttler says Brendon McCullum's removal as England Test coach may have boosted Cricket World Cup chances
articles.summary: Brendon McCullum left his role as England Test coach in July; Jos Buttler believes the move has allowed the New Zealander to focus solely on helping England win the Cricket World Cup; Buttler has been ruled out of the upcoming Pakistan white-ball tour due to injury
articles.body:
McCullum was relieved of his red-ball duties in July , with Stephen Fleming eventually named as his successor , but remained in charge of a limited-overs set-up that ended the summer with a record of 11 wins and two defeats.

That included ODI series wins over India and Sri Lanka , raising England's stock in a format that has seen them decline since they became world champions in 2019.

Buttler, who captained the team in their ill-fated 2023 title defence, thinks the split coaching model has allowed McCullum to throw all his energy towards next year's tournament in southern Africa.

"He's only got one focus now and that is the white ball," Buttler said on his For the Love of Cricket podcast.

"It's not that he couldn't do everything, because he could, but your time is more spread and you've got more to think about with the Test team as well.

"Now he can focus solely on white-ball cricket - T20, yes, but mainly ODI cricket with that World Cup on the horizon. It seems like Baz is naturally all in on, 'how do I win this World Cup with this team?'

"I think he can sort of see that World Cup is not that far away. It's a real target, now his remit has changed from four months ago being in charge of everything to, 'right, I can really nail down on this'. He's just got more time and more focus on that.

"ODI cricket for England has not been consistently great for a couple of years, so there's some nice growth to go on that and this summer's been a really good start."

Buttler delivers update on hamstring injury

Buttler is currently sidelined with a hamstring injury and has already been ruled out for the forthcoming tri-series tour of Pakistan.

He is also a doubt for the November trip to Australia, meaning the team's most experienced one-day player could miss as many as eight ODIs and a significant chunk of the pre-World Cup preparations.

"I've had a scan and I'm waiting to see the specialist. Then we'll know what the next steps are," he said.

"The unknown is often the tough part. Any cricketer just wants a physio or a doctor to tell you, 'on this date you'll be back playing cricket'. Unfortunately, they can't do that just yet."

So it remains to be seen how the management charts his route, but volume will remain the keyword.The fast bowling core identified for the New Zealand Tests comprising Mohammed Siraj, Gurnoor Brar, Prasidh Krishna, Auqib Nabi and Akash Deep will also be asked to get enough overs under their belt.Special focus will be on Akash as the team management is very excited to have him back in the set up and will closely monitor his progress starting with the Irani Cup tie in Srinagar.Another player who will be keenly tracked is all-rounder Nitish Kumar Reddy, more for his bowling because he will lend the crucial balance to the Playing XI.With Ajit Agarkar unlikely to get an extension as the chief selector, Pragyan Ojha could well chair the selection meeting when the men who matter assemble to pick squads for the tour of New Zealand. articles.body: Guwahati: With the ODI World Cup in South Africa just a year away, the Indian team management’s priority now is to identify the bowling combinations. A big part of the process is trying out different new-ball bowlers in the ongoing ODI series against West Indies.“You may see different bowlers taking the new ball because it is important for us to assess how these young players respond under pressure,” spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule said on the eve of the second ODI.It may be noted that India don’t have the services of Jasprit Bumrah for this series as he is part of the T20I team currently in the Asian Games in Japan.In the first ODI in Thiruvananthapuram, India opened the bowling with seam-bowling allrounder Nitish Kumar Reddy and Prasidh Krishna after benching Mohammed Siraj. articles.title: Supreme Court puts RCA election results on hold after 35 vote, three districts abstain
articles.summary: Jaipur: Voting for the Rajasthan Cricket Association (RCA) elections concluded here on Tuesday under the shadow of a Supreme Court directive halting the
articles.body: Jaipur: Voting for the Rajasthan Cricket Association (RCA) elections concluded here on Tuesday under the shadow of a Supreme Court directive halting the announcement of results. The apex court's stay came following petitions challenging the complete exclusion of women from the electoral rolls and a legal dispute over the inclusion of three newly formed districts in the voter list. Out of a total of 38 eligible voters, 35 cast their votes while three new districts, Didwana-Kuchaman, Khairthal-Tijara and Balotra, voluntarily refrained from polling. Following the court order, the ballot boxes were sealed and deposited in the collectorate treasury without counting, extending the state body’s long history of delayed election outcomes.The polling day was also marked by sharp exchanges between the two presidential post candidates, with Dhananjay Singh Khimsar raising questions over ‘unauthorized presence’ inside the venue and Brij Kishore Upadhyay dismissing the charges while expressing full confidence in his victory.Meanwhile, election officer AK Pandey confirmed that polling was conducted smoothly.“Voting commenced and concluded peacefully. Three new districts did not vote. They submitted in writing that they chose not to vote out of their own free will. In the meantime, we received information that the Supreme Court has issued an order directing that the results of this election should not be declared. Consequently, we have sealed the ballot box and stored it safely until further orders,” Pandey said.Khimsar questioned the presence of outsiders inside the premises and raised concerns over the decision of three districts to skip voting despite attending the AGM before the polling began.“We completely respect the decision of the Supreme Court, but we have registered a formal written complaint regarding irregularities. Why were 11 or 12 individuals who had no connection with cricket allowed entry inside the venue, despite strict identity checks at the gate, if not to influence voters? Representatives from Didwana-Kuchaman, Khairthal-Tijara and Balotra attended the AGM, but did not vote, which raises serious concerns,” Khimsar added while maintaining that there is no internal factionalism with the BJP.Upadhyay rejected the allegations of voter influence and announced plans to move the court for an early declaration of results.“RCA voting was conducted in a very peaceful manner and we fully respect the court’s decision. Regarding the allegations of unauthorized people, these are baseless claims typical during election time. The location has a common cafeteria where media and friends sit, but the polling area was completely separate. Association secretaries are experienced individuals who cannot be influenced by people sitting in a cafeteria,” Upadhyay said. “The three district associations refrained from voting voluntarily out of respect for the judiciary after learning about the court order. We plan to file an application to become a party in court to request an early declaration, and we are 100% confident of victory once the results are opened,” he added.The election officer said that there is no scope to act upon complaints. “While polling was ongoing, no complaints were received. After polling concluded, when we were busy with the sealing process, we received two or three complaints. However, at this stage, there is no scope to act upon them. Everything has now been sealed in the ballot box, and the results will be declared once permission is received from the Supreme Court,” Pandey added.Om Prakash Beniwal, representing Didwana-Kuchaman said that their decision was taken to avoid prolonging the legal dispute.“The three of us decided voluntarily that we will not participate in this voting, so that the results don’t get affected or delayed by the court for a long time,” Beniwal said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Major posting' for Shoaib Akhtar? Mohsin Naqvi holds talks with former Pakistan star
articles.summary: Former Pakistan fast bowler Shoaib Akhtar could soon move from being one of the Pakistan Cricket Board’s most vocal critics to having a role in shaping
articles.body: Former Pakistan fast bowler Shoaib Akhtar could soon move from being one of the Pakistan Cricket Board’s most vocal critics to having a role in shaping its cricketing decisions.Akhtar is reportedly in line for a major position within the PCB as chairman Mohsin Naqvi looks to restructure the board’s cricket think tank following Pakistan’s disastrous tour of England, PTI reported. While the exact nature of the proposed role has not been formally announced, Akhtar and Naqvi have already held discussions over Pakistan cricket.A source close to the PCB said Akhtar, who resides in Islamabad, met Naqvi last week and the two spoke at length about cricket-related matters.“Few weeks back when Shoaib’s elder brother passed away Mohsin Naqvi had interacted with him closely and was there for him. This gesture impressed Shoaib a lot who has been a vocal critic of the PCB and Pakistan cricket in the past in his media appearances,” the source added.The relationship between the two has since strengthened, with Naqvi also sharing his plans with Akhtar and inviting him to visit the National Cricket Academy (NCA) and training camps.“Shoaib is in line to get a major posting but obviously when he met with the Chairman he had his own set of ideas and conditions through which he believes Pakistan cricket can be taken forward,” the source said.PCB plans wider overhaulAkhtar's potential appointment comes as the PCB considers changes beyond the senior men's team. The board is also exploring the possibility of bringing in foreign coaches and consultants following the departures of senior team fielding coach Shane McDermott and batting coach Ashley Noffke.The women's national team is another area under review, with the PCB considering the appointment of a permanent long-term head coach.“The board is working on some plans for the future and there will be some changes in the cricket think tank soon because the Chairman has made it clear that he expects better results from the national mens, womens, shaheens and junior teams,” the source stated.The proposed restructuring follows a difficult period for Pakistan cricket, particularly after the men's team's Test series in England.Pakistan were beaten 3-0 in the series, suffering a first-ever clean sweep in a Test series on English soil. The result has increased scrutiny on the national side as well as the wider cricketing structure surrounding it. In the middle of the series, Pakistan sent back seven players, including Mohammed Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq, as well as head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul. Mike Hesson was subsequently asked to fill the head coach role in the third Test.The PCB is therefore examining changes to its cricketing setup, including coaching and consultancy appointments, rather than restricting its response to the senior men's team.From critic to decision-maker?Akhtar has spent years speaking publicly about Pakistan cricket, regularly questioning selection decisions, administrative choices and the direction of the national team. His outspoken views have often made him a prominent critic of the PCB.A formal role within the board would therefore mark a significant change for the former fast bowler. Instead of analysing Pakistan cricket from outside the system, Akhtar could potentially have a direct say in the decisions and plans he has frequently commented on.The precise position being considered for him, however, is yet to be formally announced.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ashwin picks Sachin over Kohli, reveals what Virat must do to be on the same level
articles.summary: Ravichandran Ashwin has spent years sharing the dressing room with both Sachin Tendulkar and Virat Kohli, but when asked to settle the never-ending debate
articles.body: Ravichandran Ashwin has spent years sharing the dressing room with both Sachin Tendulkar and Virat Kohli, but when asked to settle the never-ending debate over who is the better batsman, the former India spinner has a clear answer.For Ashwin, Tendulkar remains ahead of Kohli, and his reasoning goes beyond numbers. The era in which Tendulkar played and the enormous responsibility he carried as Indian cricket's biggest hope are central to Ashwin's argument.The Tendulkar-Kohli comparison has continued to grow as Kohli has rewritten several ODI records previously held by his idol. Kohli has already moved ahead of Tendulkar's tally of ODI centuries, while Tendulkar remains well ahead in Test cricket. Their contrasting records across formats have ensured that the debate is unlikely to disappear even after Kohli's retirement.Ashwin believes Kohli has several qualities that make him exceptional, particularly his fitness, consistency and ability to score hundreds regularly. But when it comes to pure skill, he feels Tendulkar remains unmatched.“There should never be any comparisons between Sachin Tendulkar and Virat Kohli, and every time I will stick my neck out and say, Sachin Tendulkar. On two counts. First, I am a big fan. And second, look at the kind of innings he has played. He was Indian cricket’s hope. It is not Virat Kohli’s fault. If he were to bat at No. 3 in any generation, he would have been a champion player, no doubt. But look at the rules, in the first innings, after 34 overs against West Indies in the 1st ODI, they should have played with one ball. The ball got old in daylight. Sachin Tendulkar played a lot of 50-overs cricket in day-time. We don’t play that. Five fielders are inside the circle. Two new balls. These are huge factors. And to compare people of two generations, it’s sinister in my mind,” Ashwin said on his YouTube show ‘Ash ki Baat’.There is, however, one achievement that could make Ashwin put Kohli on the same pedestal as Tendulkar.That is the elusive landmark of 100 international centuries.Kohli currently has 86 international hundreds and needs another 14 to reach the mark Tendulkar set 14 years ago. With India expected to play another 30-odd ODIs, including next year's World Cup in South Africa, the opportunity remains for Kohli to chase the record.Kohli has already said that the 2027 World Cup will be his final appearance at the tournament. Ashwin also does not expect his former captain to continue beyond that event, making the pursuit of 100 centuries particularly significant.For Ashwin, reaching that figure would transform the comparison. If Kohli manages to complete a century of international hundreds before or during the 2027 World Cup, Ashwin believes the two batting greats would finally stand on the same level.“As a well-wisher, I really wish he hangs up his boots by then (2027 World Cup) because he has committed that it will be his last World Cup. To maintain such elite level of fitness and batting requires a lot of effort, and I’m sure behind closed doors, he is continuing to put in that work. He doesn’t want to do it after that. Keeping all that in mind, logically, he can do it - score 100 centuries - and if he does, I will take my hat off. It will be a remarkable achievement. And in this home run, if he is able to do it, I would say both of them are on the same level, without a shadow of a doubt," added Ashwin.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ben Stokes: What next for the former England captain after tumultuous summer ended with success?
articles.summary: After concluding the county summer with Durham and the end of his England central contract, what is in store for Ben Stokes?
articles.body:
As cricket prepares to go into hibernation for the winter after the usual summer slog, Ben Stokes' playing diary is a lot quieter than previously.

For the first time since 2014, there will be no central contract from the England and Wales Cricket Board as he begins the next chapter of his career.

The 35-year-old caused one of the sporting stories of the year when he announced in the middle of a Test decider against New Zealand that he was walking away from the England captaincy and international cricket as a whole.

Initial sanctuary has come at his own county, Durham, where he has been a wholehearted and willing contributor to their Division Two title success.

But it is a long six months before whites will be seen around English grounds again, and it means one of the greatest all-rounders the game has ever seen - and arguably the game's best player over the past decade - is now open to offers.

Tough chats and Three Peaks - Durham's road to the title

Campbell moves to Durham director of cricket role

As England's Test team start focusing on a Christmas tour to South Africa, Stokes is heading to Australia for the festive period.

That's because he has signed to play in the Big Bash for Adelaide Strikers as he plays in the T20 competition for the first time since 2015.

From there, Stokes has a variety of options as the gates of the franchise world are open to him.

But there are also complications. A global superstar like him would surely be of interest in India, but he did not take part in the IPL's mega auction in 2025 because of England commitments.

Overseas players who have previously played in the IPL - as Stokes has done for Chennai Super Kings, Rajasthan Royals and Rising Pune Supergiant - must register for the mega-auction that takes place every three years, or miss the subsequent two mini-auctions. As things stand, that makes him ineligible until the 2028 edition.

South Africa's SA 20 begins just before the Big Bash finishes, while the Pakistan Super League, which is expected to run concurrently with the IPL in the spring, would love a headliner like Stokes to bring some stardust and eyeballs to their tournament.

Head into the summer and there is Major League Cricket in the United States. But this is where another complication may arise.

If Stokes wants to play for Durham, or signs a contract that includes any white-ball cricket in the T20 Blast or One-Day Cup, he would need a special No-Objection Certificate (NOC) from the ECB to play in a franchise league that clashes with domestic competitions for which they are contracted.

And the ECB has previously refused NOCs to former England players who have wanted to pursue freelance T20 careers.

Retirement the best thing for me - Stokes

England captain Ben Stokes announces retirement

12 Dec 2026 - 26 Jan 2027: Big Bash (Australia)

Mid-June - mid-July: Major League Cricket (USA)

And then there is his boyhood club, Durham.

It is where Stokes has wholeheartedly thrown himself into things away from the England spotlight.

After a family holiday, he returned to play in all 10 of their One-Day Cup games as they reached the semi-finals, before turning out in four of their remaining six Championship matches as the side romped to the Division Two title by 47 points, going unbeaten in the process.

There were plenty of highlights, too. He smashed an unbeaten 108 away to Derbyshire in his first game away from the international spotlight in the 50-over competition in July.

In the Championship, he hit four half-centuries in 10 innings and averaged 47.88 but it was with the ball in hand that the fireworks happened.

His rapid burst of 5-17 blew away Derbyshire again last month and, in a dead rubber at home to Worcestershire in the penultimate game, with the title already secured, Stokes produced one of his marathon spells to finish with 6-94 off 31.3 overs - the most wickets and overs of any bowler in the team.

His 25 wickets this season came at average of 20.36 and he demonstrated once again that he remains a fearsome and competitive animal when the match is on the line.

But Durham now need to discuss with Stokes how next summer will look, and it will be one of the first tasks for Ryan Campbell in his new role as director of cricket.

The Australian has spent the past four seasons as head coach, and enjoyed having Stokes in the dressing room and part of his team, and he believes that the all-rounder is keen to continue playing county cricket - and the red-ball stuff in particular.

"Yes, I do, I honestly do," Campbell told BBC Sport in an interview before his new role was announced.

"His love of the game, he talks about his bowling run-up and stuff that he can adapt to county cricket so he can bowl more. The playing, the batting, where he wants to bat, this sort of stuff, he's all-in I would have thought for the next couple of years at least."

When Stokes was suspended by the ECB for the second Test in June, it was Durham where he rediscovered his love of the game after the troubles of the Ashes in Australia last winter and the broken curfew post-Lords.

Being in and around the Riverside, singing the Blaydon Races after team victories and helping academy youngsters with practice is something that has not gone unnoticed.

"Ben's England through-and-through, but he is Durham through-and-through," said Campbell.

"He loves the club. The proudest thing I've ever had in relation to our work was when he said, 'I want to go back and play at Durham because the time there has been so amazing'. That's a big rap for our club and our environment that we've created."

But as Stokes contemplates his future, it's worth pointing out that he has not played a match in the short format of the game since appearing for Northern Superchargers in The Hundred in 2024.

While his appearances in the One-Day Cup this summer were his first in the 50-over format of white-ball cricket since the 2023 World Cup.

Of course, he has played starring roles in England winning the World Cup final in 2019 and then the World T20 final in 2022, but in the past few years he focused primarily on his commitments as England Test captain.

It is going to be a change of pace and Campbell is fascinated to see what unfolds.

"Ben will be quite wise with his decisions of where he goes, how long for, how many games he's going to play," he said.

"It's going to be a big test for him as he hasn't played T20 cricket for ages - trying to get back into the rhythm of white-ball bowling and batting.

"I hear Adelaide are going to open the batting with him. That's brilliant. That's where he belongs in T20 cricket. Where does he bowl? How are they going to use him? I'm intrigued to see that sort of stuff."

articles.title: To end 34-year Ranji drought, Punjab rope in 38-year-old Umesh Yadav as guest player | Exclusive
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Punjab are turning to experience in its quest to end a 34-year wait for the Ranji Trophy, making a significant departure from their traditional
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Punjab are turning to experience in its quest to end a 34-year wait for the Ranji Trophy, making a significant departure from their traditional approach by signing 38-year-old India pacer Umesh Yadav as a guest player for the 2026-27 domestic season. The move is historic for the Punjab Cricket Association (PCA), with Umesh becoming the first guest player signed by the association.Umesh, who has played 55 Tests, 75 ODIs and nine T20Is for India, has received a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the Vidarbha Cricket Association (VCA) and will play for Punjab this season. PCA president Amarjit Mehta confirmed the veteran pacer's move from Vidarbha to Punjab."He has proven credentials as a bowler. He has won the Ranji Trophy with Vidarbha and has been a champion bowler for India as well," Mehta told TimesofIndia.com.Asked about the decision to sign a player who will turn 39 in three weeks, and about the historic nature of the move, Mehta said: "We have taken the decision keeping our red-ball cricket in focus. Punjab have not won the Ranji Trophy since 1992 and we think Umesh is someone who can deliver us the title."His experience is going to be invaluable to the youngsters in the team. There is so much to learn from someone of Umesh's stature."Mehta also pointed to Punjab's fast-bowling resources being stretched, with Gurnoor Brar and Arshdeep Singh expected to be away on India duty."Look, our boys, whenever they are available, play for Punjab. But Gurnoor and Arshdeep will be busy with India duty, and with them gone, our bowling becomes weak. This is also one of the reasons why we have decided to bring in Umesh Yadav," he said.Umesh, who last played for India in the World Test Championship (WTC) final against Australia at The Oval in June 2023, is likely to join the Punjab Ranji Trophy camp in the next day or two."He is still fit and, in Indian conditions, along with Mohammed Shami, Umesh was lethal. I think age is just a number and Umesh ticks all the boxes when it comes to fitness," Punjab coach Amit Uniyal told this website."Having said that, there is no guarantee that he will play all the matches. A lot will depend on the combination as well. But his presence in the dressing room is going to be huge," he added.Punjab will play their first game of the Ranji Trophy season against Assam at New Chandigarh from October 11.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ILT20 Season 5 Player Auction: Big names, purse remaining and everything you need to know
articles.summary: The International League T20 (ILT20) Season 5 Player Auction will be held on Thursday, October 1, in Dubai, with more than 200 players from 23 countries
articles.body: The International League T20 (ILT20) Season 5 Player Auction will be held on Thursday, October 1, in Dubai, with more than 200 players from 23 countries set to go under the hammer. The auction pool features some of the biggest names in T20 cricket, including Babar Azam, Phil Salt, Tom Banton, Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Wanindu Hasaranga, Alzarri Joseph, Faf du Plessis and Liam Livingstone.The six franchises will enter the auction with purses ranging from $1.3 million to $1.39 million, while they must build squads of between 18 and 23 players.Here is everything you need to know about the ILT20 Season 5 auction:Q. When and where is the ILT20 Season 5 auction?The auction will be held on Thursday, October 1, 2026, at the ICC Academy Indoors in Dubai.Q. How many players are in the auction?More than 200 players from 23 countries have registered for the auction.The player pool includes cricketers from 11 ICC Full Member nations, as well as ILT20 partner nations Kuwait and Saudi Arabia and 10 other ICC Associate Member nations.Q. What are the player price categories?Players have been placed in three base-price categories:$80,000$40,000$10,000The $80,000 bracket features several established T20 names, including Babar Azam, Phil Salt, Tom Banton, David Willey, Fakhar Zaman, Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Jonny Bairstow, Moeen Ali, Liam Livingstone, Alzarri Joseph, Wanindu Hasaranga, Faf du Plessis, Alex Hales, Naseem Shah, Fazalhaq Farooqi and Chris Woakes.The $40,000 category includes Jayden Seales, Ibrahim Zadran, Shadab Khan, Tabraiz Shamsi, Avishka Fernando, Kusal Perera, Gulbadin Naib, Chris Green and Andre Fletcher.The $10,000 bracket features players such as Will Smeed, Lorcan Tucker, Reeza Hendricks, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Ish Sodhi, George Munsey, Matt Potts, Bas de Leede and Tanzim Hasan Sakib.Q. How the $10,000 category could be decisive in shaping the squads?The lowest base-price category could play an important role in squad building, particularly because franchises have significant roster requirements to fulfil.All players from UAE, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia will enter the auction at a base price of $10,000.Q. Why are UAE players expected to attract attention?UAE, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia players could not be retained by franchises under the Season 5 recruitment rules.That means several established Gulf-region players will return to the auction pool, including UAE internationals Muhammad Waseem, Junaid Siddique, Haider Ali, Ayan Afzal Khan, Alishan Sharafu and Khuzaima Tanveer.Franchises will also have the option of using one Right to Match (RTM) on a UAE player who either represented them in Season 4 or played for them in the recently concluded ILT20 Development Tournament.Q. How much money does each franchise have to spend?Each team receives a base auction purse of $1.3 million, with any remaining money from the $700,000 allocated for pre-auction signings added to that purse.The available purses are:MI Emirates: $1.39mAbu Dhabi Knight Riders: $1.365mDesert Vipers: $1.305mGulf Giants: $1.305mDubai Capitals: $1.30mSharjah Warriorz: $1.30mQ. What are the squad-size requirements?Every franchise must finish the auction with a minimum of 18 players and a maximum of 23 players.Each squad must contain:At least 11 players from ICC Full Member countriesAt least four Afghanistan playersAt least one Ireland playerAt least four UAE playersAt least one Kuwait playerAt least one Saudi Arabia playerAt least one additional ICC Associate player, excluding UAE, Kuwait and Saudi ArabiaQ. How much must franchises spend?Each team must spend at least $1.5 million and no more than $2 million on its squad.After the auction, franchises can sign one Wildcard player for an additional maximum fee of $250,000.Q. What are the playing XI requirements?Every playing XI in Season 5 must include:At least two UAE playersAt least two Afghanistan playersAt least one additional Associate Member playerThe additional Associate slot can be filled by a third UAE player or a player from another Associate nation, including Kuwait or Saudi Arabia.Q. What happens if a player withdraws from the auction?All replacement players must have registered for the Season 5 auction.Any player who withdraws from the auction on or before October 1 will not be eligible to participate in Season 5 either as a replacement player or as a Wildcard signing.Q. What are the six franchises taking into the auction?Abu Dhabi Knight Riders: $1.365mCurrent squad: Finn Allen, Jason Holder, Matthew Tromp, Sunil Narine.They still need to acquire four UAE players, eight Full Member players, one Kuwait player and one Saudi Arabia player.Desert Vipers: $1.305mCurrent squad: Andries Gous, Dan Lawrence, Mujeeb-ur-Rahman, Shimron Hetmyer.They still need four UAE players, eight Full Member players, one Kuwait player and one Saudi Arabia player.Dubai Capitals: $1.30mCurrent squad: Marcus Stoinis, Mustafizur Rahman, Noor Ahmad, Rovman Powell.They still need four UAE players, seven Full Member players, one Associate player, one Kuwait player and one Saudi Arabia player.Gulf Giants: $1.305mCurrent squad: Azmatullah Omarzai, Blessing Muzarabani, David Miller, Heinrich Klaasen.They still need four UAE players, seven Full Member players, one Associate player, one Kuwait player and one Saudi Arabia player.MI Emirates: $1.39mCurrent squad: Nicholas Pooran, Rashid Khan, Romario Shepherd, Sherfane Rutherford.They still need four UAE players, seven Full Member players, one Associate player, one Kuwait player and one Saudi Arabia player.Sharjah Warriorz: $1.30mCurrent squad: Adam Milne, James Vince, Waqar Salamkheil, Sikandar Raza.They still need four UAE players, seven Full Member players, one Associate player, one Kuwait player and one Saudi Arabia player.Q. Where to live stream the auction?The Season 5 Player Auction will be streamed live on the official ILT20 YouTube channel. In India, the live stream will also be available on Zee5.Q. articles.body: West Indies opener John Campbell hit a century off just 65 balls in the second ODI against India at the Barsapara Cricket Stadium in Guwahati on Wednesday, giving his team a strong start as they look to level the three-match series.West Indies had lost the first ODI by eight wickets, but Campbell’s innings put them in a strong position early in the second game while batting first.The left-handed batter reached his century in the 17th over with a single off India spinner Kuldeep Yadav, who had been the standout bowler in the first ODI.
